techniques.name: Motivated Push-In
techniques.core_mechanism: Constricts frame boundary around focal subject to amplify narrative gravity, internal realization, and eliminate peripheral distractions.

variants.slow_creep: 1.5s–3.5s smooth forward drift → Deepens intimacy, vulnerability, mounting dread
variants.snap_crash: 0.1s–0.3s digital punch-in (1.15x) → Accents comedy punchline, shock, or eureka moment
variants.snap_punch: 0.1s–0.3s digital punch-in (1.15x) accenting punchlines, revelations, or shock

use_when: Narrative pivots from external context to internal realization
Dialogue transitions from casual setup to high-stakes confession
Audience attention must isolate a micro-expression or critical prop
Character notices a critical detail or experiences an internal realization
Directing audience attention to subtle facial shift or prop
avoid_when: Shot duration is under 1.2s (insufficient time for drift to register)
Scene demands clinical emotional detachment or observational distance
Unmotivated by subject action, dialogue change, or sonic shift

Movement is unmotivated by subject action or dialogue

techniques.name: Revealing Pull-Out

variants.isolation_reveal: Slow reverse dolly from close-up to wide → Emphasizes loneliness or vulnerability
variants.spatial_punch: Fast snap pull-out → Sudden shock reveal of surprising environment or companion

techniques.name: Kinetic Whip Pan
techniques.core_mechanism: High-velocity rotation blurs frame boundaries, transferring kinetic energy directly into the subsequent scene.

variants.teleport_snap: 180-degree blur cut between two different physical locations
variants.reaction_whip: Violent rotational whip from speaker to reacting listener

use_when: Connecting disparate scenes in high-tempo comedic or travel montages
Eliminating perceived dead space between two dialogue lines
Creating a kinetic, stylized sense of urgency
Eliminating perceived dead space between dialogue lines
avoid_when: Subdued, contemplative, or somber narrative beats
Used more than twice in 15s (causes visual fatigue)
When audience needs to comprehend subtle background geography

techniques.name: Kinetic Handheld Drift
techniques.core_mechanism: Organic micro-movements convey human presence, immediacy, and psychological proximity.

variants.organic_float: Subtle breathing motion → Authentic conversational intimacy
variants.visceral_shake: Aggressive handheld motion → Physical chaos, urgency, panic

use_when: Authentic vlogs, travel verité, or documentary reality
Subject is physically moving, walking, or actively building
Breaking robotic studio stiffness to establish creator trust
avoid_when: Fine macro product demos requiring crisp stability
Corporate explainer requiring formal, authoritative polish

techniques.name: First-Person Subjective POV
techniques.core_mechanism: Places lens in first-person eye perspective directly over hands interacting with objects, crafts, or tools.

variants.hands_in_frame: Creator's hands manipulating tools or food in foreground → Tactile immersion
variants.walking_gaze: Looking around corners, up at monuments, or into crowds → Exploratory curiosity
variants.over_the_shoulder: OTS angle establishing creator presence and subject focus
variants.first_person_craft: Top-down or chest-mounted POV showing hands manipulating material

use_when: Tutorial demonstrations where viewer replicates creator's exact actions
Travel arrivals where audience explores a new street through creator's eyes
Unboxing or tactile craft sequences
Demonstrating physical skill, cooking step, or technical teardown
Inviting viewer to feel somatic ownership of the action
Showing physical obstacles or tactile textures up close
avoid_when: High-emotion dialogue where facial micro-expressions are essential
When creator's face and personal charisma carry the retention
Abstract conceptual or philosophical exposition
Emotional conversational moments requiring facial expressions

techniques.name: Geometric / Action Match Cut
techniques.core_mechanism: Bridges two distinct scenes by aligning identical visual geometry, action direction, or subject framing across the cut boundary.

variants.action_match: Motion initiated in Scene A completes fluidly in Scene B → Seamless spatial teleportation
variants.graphic_match: Identical shape or silhouette on screen (e.g. coffee mug → sunrise) → Poetic thematic linkage
variants.object_handover: Item tossed toward camera in scene A caught in scene B
variants.directional_stride: Footstep or hand swipe continuing motion seamlessly into new setting

use_when: Transitioning across a time jump or location change without losing narrative momentum
Drawing a symbolic parallel between two disparate subjects or events
Fast montage sequences where continuous motion disguises scene cuts
Transitioning between disparate locations or time periods
Elevating visual craft and rewarding attentive viewer gaze
Compressing extensive real-time travel or preparation
avoid_when: Subtle emotional scenes where conspicuous visual cleverness distracts from dialogue
When subject alignment is slightly misregistered (feels like an accidental jump cut)
Disorienting sequences where spatial confusion is the objective
When source clips lack matching physical momentum

techniques.name: J-Cut Audio Lead
techniques.core_mechanism: Next scene's dialogue or sound arrives 0.4s–0.8s before visual cut, psychologically pulling viewer curiosity forward.

variants.dialogue_bleed: Upcoming voiceover spoken before scene cut → Eliminates hesitation drop-off
variants.ambient_anticipation: Loud environment audio arrives while still on quiet scene → Pre-primes audience
variants.dialogue_pre_lap: Voice begins speaking over current visuals before cutting to speaker face
variants.sound_anticipation: Crashing waves or subway sounds before camera shows new setting

use_when: Preventing viewer swipe-away at scene transition boundaries
Smoothing abrupt jumps between talking head and B-roll action
Introducing an off-screen interruption or sudden arrival
Softening abrupt scene transitions to feel organically cinematic
Pulling viewer curiosity forward into next narrative scene
Building acoustic anticipation for off-screen arrival
avoid_when: Moments of sharp simultaneous audiovisual shock

Abrupt comedy slap cuts designed to produce sudden jarring shocks

techniques.name: Scale & Energy Contrast Cut
techniques.core_mechanism: Abrupt cut from extreme close-up (ECU) directly to extreme wide (EW), violently resetting spatial perspective.

variants.macro_to_infinity: Extreme close-up macro texture cut directly to extreme wide landscape
variants.kinetic_to_still: High-velocity motion cut to dead-stop frozen subject
variants.micro_to_macro: Tight shot of fingers trembling transitioning to vast empty city square
variants.shock_isolation: Wide crowd shot transitioning to suffocating macro close-up of sweating brow

use_when: Breaking monotonous pacing at the 5s–8s retention cliff
Dramatizing the difference between expectation and reality
Punching in for maximum comedic or shock emphasis
Juxtaposing personal vulnerability against massive external world
Injecting sudden visual scale after claustrophobic dialogue
Surprising viewer expectations at narrative turning points
avoid_when: Gentle, meditative, or continuous single-action sequences
Overused back-to-back (disorients spatial comprehension)
Continuous instructional tutorials requiring steady visual context
Subtle dialogue exchanges between conversational partners

techniques.name: Cadence Jump Cut
techniques.core_mechanism: Removes breath pauses and non-essential syllables within the same continuous shot to create breathless velocity.

variants.audio_gap_removal: Trimming audio pauses down to < 0.1s → Relentless information density
variants.framing_punch_jump: Alternating between 1.0x and 1.15x scale across speech cuts → Dynamic visual pop
variants.angle_alternator: Alternating 1.0x and 1.15x crop every sentence to hide cut seams
variants.rapid_progression: Rapid succession of short sub-second cuts showing progressive assembly

use_when: Opening 0-3s hook to pack maximum thesis into minimum runtime

Direct-to-camera monologues needing high energetic momentum
High-energy explainer, comedic vlog, or educational breakdown
Condensing complex narrative without dropping vocal momentum
Preventing retention drop during expository bridges
avoid_when: Vulnerable, poetic, or tragic storytelling requiring contemplative breathing room

techniques.name: Visual Motif Anchor
techniques.core_mechanism: Repeats a single physical prop, framing setup, or color cue across distinct story phases to visualize internal transformation.

variants.temporal_anchor: Same object held at start, middle, and end → Visual proof of time passed and habits built
variants.emotional_barometer: State of object degrades or improves alongside creator's journey → Physical metaphor for emotional state
variants.prop_talisman: Holding the same coffee mug, notebook, or camera in 3 distinct city settings
variants.habitual_gesture: Same breath check, shoe tying, or watch tap opening and closing the piece

Providing emotional grounding amidst chaotic external progression
Tying ending shot back to opening hook in a satisfying narrative loop

When the chosen object lacks organic narrative connection to the creator's subject

techniques.name: Delayed Spatial Reveal
techniques.core_mechanism: Deliberately withholds the full environment through tight framing, building curious tension before revealing where the creator actually is.

variants.macro_tease: Extreme close-up on hands doing a mundane action, then pulling wide to reveal an extraordinary setting (e.g. edge of a cliff)
variants.reflection_reveal: Opening on a mirror or glass reflection before camera steps out into the real room
variants.fake_studio_reveal: Creator talking in pristine frame before cut reveals chaotic clutter behind camera
variants.false_intimacy: Tight frame appears solitary before cut reveals crowded public train

Surprise travel destination reveals
Challenging audience assumptions before delivering the punchline
Subverting expectations with comedic or dramatic irony
Creating curiosity gap about where action takes place
Delivering a twist punchline based on physical location
avoid_when: When the location is ordinary and the reveal produces anti-climax
Educational tutorials where spatial confusion frustrates the learner
Factual documentary requiring immediate authentic location proof
Fast montages where spatial withholding feels confusing rather than witty

techniques.name: Subject Isolation Contrast
techniques.core_mechanism: Frames the creator static while surrounding environment blurs with motion or crowd chaos, externalizing internal alienation.

variants.motion_blur_crowd: Slow shutter or high crowd flow moving past stationary creator
variants.negative_space_wide: Subject occupies under 10% of frame surrounded by massive empty architectural scale
variants.time_lapse_freeze: Subject still while timelapse crowd streams around them
variants.shallow_depth_isolation: Subject in sharp focus while rushing crowd is thrown into soft bokeh

techniques.name: Pre-Reveal Sudden Silence
techniques.core_mechanism: Cuts background music and ambient audio completely to create vacuum tension before a climax, punchline, or realization.

variants.micro_vacuum: 0.3s–0.5s total audio drop immediately before visual impact → Maximizes punchline contrast
variants.extended_hush: 1.0s–2.0s silence with subtle breathing/room tone → Signals high vulnerability or shock
variants.needle_drop_hush: Music cuts abruptly leaving only creator breath or room tone
variants.sound_vacuum: Fades frequencies into hollow muffled vacuum before sonic slam

techniques.name: Syncopated SFX Impact
techniques.core_mechanism: Syncs concrete, high-frequency sound effects (whoosh, click, mechanical snap, sub-bass thump) to visual changes to stimulate auditory reward.

variants.tactile_snap: Cut synced with physical impact (door slam, knife chop, glass tap)
variants.whoosh_slam: Cut punctuated by low-end riser followed by instantaneous impact

techniques.name: Tension Riser Crescendo
